sources.entry: GraphHopper - Fast routing library and server using OpenStreetMap. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: GraphHopper is a fast, memory-efficient routing engine (Java library or standalone web server) that calculates routes, distances, times and turn-by-turn instructions using OpenStreetMap data.
summary.what_it_does: It computes routes between two or more points with distance, time, turn-by-turn instructions and road attributes, and also supports snap-to-road, isochrone calculation, and shortest path trees. It uses OpenStreetMap and GTFS data by default, plus elevation data, and can import other data sources. It can be run as a standalone web server with a built-in web UI (GraphHopper Maps) or embedded in Java applications via Maven. The engine offers speed mode (Contraction Hierarchies, fast with predefined profiles), flexible mode (no preparation, per-request customization), and hybrid mode, and can switch between them at request time when preparations exist. It also provides map matching for snapping GPX traces to roads and a web API with polyline encoding and GZIP.
use_cases: embedding routing in a Java application
how_to_run: Download an OpenStreetMap extract, e.g. berlin-latest.osm.pbf
Wait for the 'Server - Started' log message, then open the local web UI in a browser
Alternatively, add the graphhopper-core Maven dependency to a Java project
notable: Speed mode with Contraction Hierarchies, flexible mode, and hybrid mode, switchable per request
Pre-built vehicle profiles (car, bike, foot, truck, bus, motorcycle, etc.) with custom models for customization
Time-dependent public transit routing and GTFS reading
Turn instructions in more than 45 languages
Apache License 2.0, allowing embedding in closed-source products
caveats: Requires Java 25 or newer to run
Offline mobile routing (Android/iOS) is no longer officially supported
Route Optimization, Matrix, and hosted Directions API are commercial offerings from GraphHopper GmbH, not part of the open source engine
